global_organization_chain: global pollution and energy shortage -> eight questions -> three question clusters -> SSDM, CM, and LPM outputs
architecture figure -> economic SSDM -> static bound -> dynamic CM -> environmental/resource LPM
price-production trend change -> buyer/seller/balance regimes -> separate fitting periods -> coefficients
equilibrium calculation -> 2006 comparator -> limited reliability claim -> tax and oil analysis
tax result -> static-model omissions stated immediately -> bounded interpretation
PHEV fails to reduce oil greatly -> remaining travel benefit -> oil-consuming efficiency -> reserve projection

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Expose model ownership and handoffs before equations.
Compare price, oil supply, and travel demand under vehicle substitution.
Show the projected oil-stock consequence of the efficiency switch.
Convert installed capacity into a charging-margin bound.
Connect charging time to usable capacity.
Inspect in-sample fit quality.
Read saturation behavior and compare it with system plausibility.
Turn a fitted coefficient into a lever-sensitivity interface.
Make the LP source-sector topology visible.
Expose why the ideal optimum is unrealistic and how constraints repair it.
Show the environment-feasibility tradeoff.
Identify a shared technology-efficiency decision boundary.
Connect efficiency improvement to environmental cost and diminishing benefit.
Make the preferred vehicle type conditional on technology efficiency.
Show that vehicle type changes upstream energy distribution.
Anchor the equilibrium and efficiency comparison.
Connect tax perturbation to vehicle demand direction.
Supply the static EV upper-bound calculation.
Tie electricity capacity to a supply-demand state.
Translate fitted parameters into mechanisms.
Expose the real-capacity repair set.
Create type-specific LP comparisons.
Keep the regime-specific equations and defect auditable.
Expose the SSDM result-to-metric-to-capacity handoffs.
Keep signs, equilibrium, fit, and levers in one auditable chain.
Make feasibility, objective, and type modifications inspectable.
